# Poisson distribution {#sec-poisson}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}
$$
P(X = k) = \frac{\lambda^k e^{-\lambda}}{k!}
$${#eq-poisson}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Poisson Distribution - Probability Mass Function with different lambda parameters"
#| label: fig-poisson-dist

# Set up the plot
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1, 45), ylim = c(0, 0.25),
     xlab = "x", ylab = "P(X = x)",
     main = "Poisson Distribution - Probability Mass Function")

# Define colors and parameters
colors <- c("blue", "red", "green")
lambdas <- c(4, 10, 20)

# Plot each distribution
for (i in seq_along(lambdas)) {
  lambda <- lambdas[i]
  color <- colors[i]

  # Set reasonable upper limit for x based on lambda
  max_x <- qpois(0.9999, lambda)
  x <- 0:max_x
  pmf <- dpois(x, lambda)

  # Connect points with thin lines and add points
  lines(x, pmf, col = color, lwd = 1, lty = 1)
  points(x, pmf, pch = 21, bg = color, col = color, cex = 1.2)
}

# Add legend
legend("topright",
       legend = c("λ=4", "λ=10", "λ=20"),
       col = colors,
       lwd = 2,
       pch = 21,
       pt.bg = colors,
       cex = 0.9)

# Add grid for better readability
grid()
```
